concerns.text: T103 mandates `statistical_report.json` with "top-level keys `p_values` and `t_statistics` (one entry per outcome)" while also claiming "validity_status matching the output contract" — but contracts/output.schema.yaml requires a flat per-comparison object with keys `comparison_name`, `p_value`, `p_value_corrected`, `effect_size`, `effect_size_ci_lower/upper`, `significance_status`, `mdes`, `adjustment_status`, `validity_status`. The two structures are mutually exclusive; an implementer cannot produce a file satisfying both, and the verification clause ("every numeric field traces to the CSV") does not say which schema wins. Name the authoritative structure.

T102's column mapping normalizes to `MMSE` (and spec input schema says `MMSE`: float), but the dataset contract requires the field named `mmse_score` (integer, 0–30). An implementer following T102 verbatim produces `final_cleaned_dataset.csv` files that fail the contract schema. The task must state the canonical column name and type so the mapping table is deterministic.

openml.datasets.get_dataset(id) for the best match" is not deterministic — "best match" is undefined (no ranking rule, no tie-break, no minimum-column criteria). Two implementers can fetch different datasets. Specify the selection rule (e.g., keyword priority order, then largest row count, then lowest dataset id) so the fetch recipe in metadata.json is reproducible.

T104 evaluates per-threshold significance "using the corrected p-values from T103" but flags `is_sensitive_to_threshold` on "any raw p" in 0.04–0.06. FR-005 does not say which p-family the borderline rule applies to. State explicitly (raw vs corrected) so `test_sensitivity_sweep` has an unambiguous expected behavior.

T110 writes hashes to `state/state.yaml`, but the constitution mandates checksums in `state/projects/PROJ-524-the-impact-of-nostalgia-on-cognitive-fle.yaml` under `artifact_hashes`. The task targets a different state file than the constitution requires; the verification ("identical hashes") cannot confirm constitution compliance. Align the path.

T106's verification says "`data/stimuli_checksums.json` ... exist with the documented content", but the task body only describes writing `data/citation_status.json` and recording `WARN_STIMULI_ABSENT` in metadata.json — no step produces `stimuli_checksums.json` in the empty-stimuli branch. Specify what that file contains when stimuli are absent (e.g., `{"status": "absent"}`) or drop it from verification.
